Texas.lead: Texas sets the sale rules statewide, so they are the same in every county:
items: Mortgage foreclosures are usually nonjudicial trustee sales. Notice must be posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk at least 21 days before the sale (Property Code 51.002). Texas foreclosure guide
Sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. at the courthouse or an area the commissioners court designates, or online if the county authorizes it.

Tax sales follow a court judgment or tax warrant and are run by the sheriff or a constable. Homestead and ag property can be redeemed for 2 years, other property for 180 days (Tax Code 34.21). Texas tax sale guide

Oklahoma.lead: Oklahoma sets these rules statewide; each county's treasurer, sheriff and district court carry them out:
items: Land with taxes unpaid 3 or more years is sold at the county treasurer's resale on the second Monday of June (68 O.S. 3105, 3125). Oklahoma tax sale guide
Mortgage foreclosures usually go through district court and end in a sheriff's sale held at least 30 days after the first published notice (12 O.S. 764). Oklahoma foreclosure guide
Unless appraisal was waived, sheriff's sale bids must reach two-thirds of the appraised value, and the court must confirm the sale. Oklahoma sheriff sale guide

counties.name: Harris County
counties.answer: Harris County is a Texas county with an estimated 5,045,026 residents (Census Bureau, July 1, 2025); its county seat is Houston. Like every Texas county, it holds foreclosure and tax sales on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Property values come from the appraisal district, and foreclosure notices are filed with the county clerk.

First Tuesday of the month, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. (first Wednesday if that Tuesday is Jan. 1 or July 4)
